trial_title: Early Warning and Optimization Strategy in Carotid Endarterectomy
brief_summary: Carotid endarterectomy has been proven effective in prevention of cerebral vascular events in patients with severe carotid artery stenosis (symptomatic,\>50%;asymptomatic,60%). But during the surgery, when the carotid artery is clipping, the patient will have the chance to have hypoperfusion or stroke. Our study is designed to determine how to use TCD to reduce the risk of death and nonfatal stroke in patients .

eligibility_table.criterion: Carotid artery stenosis detectable by duplex ultrasound, and no previous procedure done on it, which might well need procedural treatment now with CEA or CAS.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has significant bilateral carotid stenosis (80% and 90%), but has undergone prior procedures (CABG) which may affect eligibility for new interventions.

eligibility_table.criterion: Already started any appropriate medical treatment (eg, statin, aspirin etc), and already recovered from any necessary coronary procedures (eg, CABG)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has undergone CABG and is likely on appropriate medical treatment for CAD, although specific medications are not listed.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient seems fit and willing for follow-up in person (at 1 month) and by annual letter (for at least 5 years)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient appears fit for follow-up, but the willingness for in-person visits is not explicitly stated.

eligibility_table.criterion: Some type of angiography (eg, MRA or CTA) has already been done that has shown that CEA.
eligibility_table.justification: There is no indication that an angiography (MRA or CTA) has been performed to show the need for CEA.

eligibility_table.criterion: Small likelihood of worthwhile benefit (eg, very low risk of stroke because stenosis is very minor, or major co-morbidity or life-threatening disease, such as advanced cancer)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has multiple significant comorbidities, but the specific risk of stroke due to stenosis is not detailed, making it uncertain but not outright excluded.
